title: Tea at Mutanabbi
logline: An English photographer new to Baghdad stops at Abu Haidar's tea stall on Mutanabbi Street. A simple request for tea leads to a warm moment of hospitality and connection.
synopsis: A bright, sunny morning illuminates Mutanabbi Street, where the air is a thick blend of old book dust and brewing tea. Clara Hughes, an English photographer with a vintage camera slung across her chest, wanders through the bustle, her eyes wide with curiosity at the historic architecture and the stacks of second-hand books.

brief.text: On a sunny morning Clara, an English photographer new to Baghdad, stops at Abu Haidar's tea stall on Mutanabbi Street. She asks in English whether this is the famous tea; he answers warmly in Iraqi Arabic and pours her a glass; she tastes it and thanks him. One continuous moment at the counter, three short shots.

scenes.title: A Taste of Mutanabbi

lines.text: Excuse me, is this the famous tea everyone talks about?

beats.action: Clara steps up to the wooden counter of the tea stall, her vintage camera on her chest, and points at the tulip-shaped tea glasses with a hopeful smile. Abu Haidar, behind the counter beside the brass samovar, looks up from polishing a glass.

lines.text: هلا بيج عيني، هذا أطيب چاي ببغداد. تفضلي اگعدي.

beats.action: Abu Haidar chuckles warmly, takes a tulip glass and pours dark amber tea from the brass samovar, then sets it on a saucer in front of Clara.

lines.text: Oh, that is wonderful. Thank you!

beats.action: Clara lifts the glass with both hands, takes a careful sip, and her face lights up; she smiles at Abu Haidar.

scenes.purpose: To establish a warm first encounter between Clara and Abu Haidar through the shared experience of traditional tea.
scenes.emotionalObjective: Create a feeling of hospitality and cross-cultural connection.
scenes.entryState: Clara approaches the wooden counter, looking curiously at the samovar; Abu Haidar is polishing a glass.
scenes.exitState: Clara is smiling and satisfied after tasting the tea; Abu Haidar is beaming with hospitality.

shots.prompt: A sun-drenched outdoor tea stall on Mutanabbi Street with an old brick arcade and book tables in the background. A slim woman in her early thirties with auburn hair in a ponytail, wearing an olive green field jacket and a vintage camera on her chest, approaches the wooden counter from the left. Behind the counter, a plump older man with salt-and-pepper thinning hair, apple-cheeks, and a white dishdasha with a red-and-white keffiyeh on his shoulder looks up from polishing a glass. He has gold-rimmed glasses on a cord around his neck. The wooden counter holds a brass samovar and rows of clear tulip-shaped tea glasses. The camera pushes in slowly as the woman speaks with a hopeful, curious expression.

beats.action: Clara steps up to the wooden counter, her vintage camera bouncing slightly on her chest.
She points to the tulip glasses with a hopeful smile; Abu Haidar stops polishing and looks up.
